specs.caption: The skip connection is an express lane for gradients: even when the layer stack crawls, the signal still arrives fresh, which is why hundred-layer networks finally trained.

specs.anchorText: let one module compute $1 \times 1$, $3 \times 3$, and $5 \times 5$ convolutions in parallel

One clear visual metaphor: an Inception module looks at several scales at once and concatenates the results, with one-by-one bottlenecks keeping the wide module affordable. Comic strip or XKCD-inspired infographic style, expressive characters, minimal clutter, tasteful and inclusive, suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image.
specs.alt: A cutaway workshop with four parallel benches where cartoon workers inspect the same image through different sized magnifying lenses, with funnels squeezing wide token streams thin before the larger benches and one shared conveyor merging all outputs, picturing the Inception module computing several filter scales in parallel with cheap one-by-one channel bottlenecks.
specs.caption: Why pick a kernel size when you can run several at once? Inception looks at every scale in parallel and lets a cheap one-by-one bottleneck keep the bill down.

specs.anchorText: a per-channel spatial filter and a $1 \times 1$ channel mix
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm soft color palette on a clean white background, generous margins: on the left, one overworked cartoon robot juggling far too many colored balls at once and sweating, labelled by visual only as the expensive all-in-one worker. A friendly arrow points right to two relaxed specialist robots who split the job: the first robot calmly stamps a pattern onto each colored ball one color at a time (the per-channel spatial step), and the second robot stands at a small mixing board blending the colors together (the one-by-one channel mix). The two specialists look efficient and unhurried. One clear visual metaphor: depthwise-separable convolution factors one costly operation into two cheap, focused steps. Comic strip or XKCD-inspired infographic style, expressive characters, gentle humor, minimal clutter, tasteful and inclusive, suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image.
specs.alt: One sweating overworked robot juggling many colored balls at once on the left, and on the right two relaxed specialist robots splitting the work, one stamping a pattern onto each color separately and one blending the colors at a mixing board, picturing how depthwise-separable convolution factors a costly dense convolution into a per-channel spatial filter plus a one-by-one channel mix.
specs.caption: Split the one expensive job into two cheap specialists, a per-channel filter and a channel mixer, and you delete about nine of every ten multiply-adds with barely a dent in accuracy.
